column3: Close to the Hebrew; the place name בַּכְּפִירִים (“Kephirim”) is translated “among the villages.”
Close to the Hebrew; the form וְגַשְׁמוּ (“Gashmu”) is normalized to “Geshem.”
NKJV supplies the address “O God” before “strengthen my hands,” which the Hebrew lacks.
NKJV renders עָצוּר (“shut up, confined”) as “a secret informer,” an interpretation; it also supplies “indeed.”
Close to the Hebrew; “and he will live” is rendered “to save his life.”
NKJV reads “saw these things” (as from the verb “see”) where the vowels give “they were afraid”; “fell greatly in their own eyes” becomes “very disheartened.”
Close to the Hebrew; בַּעֲלֵי שְׁבוּעָה (“lords of oath”) is rendered “pledged to him.”
